schemes.name: C · Prow & Lantern
schemes.tag: recommended · four buildings on one lane · prow · lantern + twin pod · wedge
schemes.blurb: Arrival at the west notch, then one gravel lane runs from the parking to the gathering cabin’s front stair, and every porch opens onto it. The lot-width rule caps all buildings at 57 ft across the lot, so the buildings sit in two rows inside that band: the family cabin on the uphill side looking down the lot toward Mud Bay, the elders’ cabin on the downhill side, and the gathering cabin at the seaward end with its prow aimed down the bay. Family sleeping (487 sq ft): two one-storey pods under one covered porch and breezeway, each household with its own front door. The octagonal lantern pod (Maya, Ren, Leo, Ana) has a hall from the porch, the parents’ room on the water side, the bunk room across the back and a bath on the west flat; the twin pod (Daniel, Sofia) has their two rooms either side of an entry and bath core under a butterfly roof. Every bedroom has a bed and a dresser, every bath its own toilet and sink clearances. Elders’ wedge (441 sq ft, Elena and Tomas): one level, every room off a 5-ft entry hall. The sitting room is on the water and gathering side, with a side door onto a level, railed boardwalk straight to the gathering porch; the accessible bath (60×60 curbless shower, 5-ft turning space) is at the front with a door from the hall and an en-suite door from the bedroom; the bedroom runs across the back with a 3-ft clear path on both sides of the bed and a glazed door to their private covered porch, which the sitting room also opens onto. Arrival is step-free: a level 4-ft boardwalk runs from the drop-off along the front wall to the covered entry (the drop-off’s east edge is graded about 6 in to meet it). Gathering prow: entry and mudroom off the lane, kitchen beside the covered outdoor kitchen, dining for 8 by the east windows, lounge in the prow, hearth between. The cabin is set 4 ft into the slope. Its prow is curved on the west, where the lounge wall and the roof sweep round toward the madrone, and sharp on the east. One deck runs under the side porch and wraps the prow; steps run all the way round the curve, 21 in treads you can sit on, flowing round the madrone’s trunk down to the firepit at their foot; the straight east side keeps its railing. The elders reach the side porch on their own sweeping boardwalk, a 1:21 slope with no steps. 1,599 of 1,600 sq ft enclosed. Sited to the 35-ft reduced setback from top of bank; slide it to 50 to see the strict case.

schemes.blurb: Scheme C with a shell roof: the prow roof reaches out over the deck to a point near its front edge, dipping toward the tip on a single slim column, so the seaward deck is covered. Inside there is no flat ceiling: it follows the cone and hips of the roof, with a band of clerestory glass between the wall tops and the vault. Everything else as C.

floors.name: Main floor · Maya, Ren, Leo & Ana

schemes.name: A · Octagon Hearth
schemes.tag: octagon · splayed pods · pyramid & butterfly roofs
schemes.blurb: The gathering cabin is a 30-ft octagon under a pyramid roof with the kitchen island dead centre, so cooking is the hearth everything radiates from: dining in the water-side bay, lounge to the west, pantry and powder room in the east facets, a sheltered entry facet on the uphill side with the stair. A three-sided covered porch hangs off the front with a stair down to the firepit and beach path. The family cabin is a skewed core (bath, bunks, hall) with two bedroom pods splayed 25° apart under opposed shed roofs, so Maya & Ren and Daniel & Sofia face different views and never share a wall. The elders’ cabin is a bay-fronted hip-roof box on a slab at grade with a ramp at the uphill door and a level link deck to the octagon.

schemes.name: B · Fan Court
schemes.blurb: The gathering cabin is a trapezoid that fans open toward the water under a butterfly roof, so the glass wall at the wide end is 33 ft of view and the roof valley throws rain to one scupper; kitchen at the narrow uphill end with an octagonal entry porch and stair, a covered dining porch across the wide end with a stair to the firepit. The elders’ cabin is a 22-ft octagon on a slab at grade with a ramp at the uphill door, a pyramid roof, a bay porch toward the court and a level link deck to the gathering cabin. The family cabin is an L with a tall gable over the parents’ side and a cross-wing for Daniel and Sofia, turned to look east over the court. The three fan around one outdoor room: firepit terrace, dining porch, beach path.

schemes.name: D · Nautilus & Kelp
schemes.tag: dream scheme · rules off · log-spiral shell · kelp-bladder pods · river stone · ribbon bridge
schemes.blurb: A dream scheme that sets the rubric aside (rules off: about 2,400 sq ft, past the setback, over the cap) to show what “really organic” could mean on this lot. You arrive at the west notch on a kidney-shaped shell-gravel court; a creek-like ribbon walk meanders downhill through camas meadow and river-stone boulders, and the elders get their own level railed boardwalk from the cars. Kelp pods (family, about 850 sq ft) is a sod-roofed gallery that bends along the contour like a kelp stipe, with four copper-domed bladder pods hanging off its bay side. Sofia and Daniel each get a teardrop pod, Leo & Ana a round bunk pod and Maya & Ren the big pod with a slider to the view; a domed bath pod and the entry sit on the uphill back. Elders’ river stone (Elena & Tomas, 500 sq ft) is a sod pebble bermed into the slope on a slab, with a sitting room, a bedroom onto a kidney porch, an accessible bath with a curbless shower and a wardrobe. A ribbon bridge leaves their sitting room, stays perfectly level as it floats over the rain-garden pond and lands on the Nautilus’s entry porch. The Nautilus (gathering, about 930 sq ft) is one whorl of a logarithmic spiral standing on raking stilts at the bank lip. Its coil’s eye rises as a copper-domed hearth room, the kitchen and dining wrap the spiral, and the open mouth is a 30-ft glass lounge facing Mud Bay under a copper shell roof that curls up like the lip of a wave. A cantilevered crescent deck and kidney balcony drop by a long stair to a creek walk past the madrones to a teardrop tide-pool sauna on stilts, then to an ocean plunge pool at the beach. All four madrones are kept, and new fir, cedar and alder are planted.

schemes.name: E · Under the Meadow
schemes.tag: dream scheme · rules off · earth-sheltered · sod roofs · hall under the hill · madrone ring
schemes.blurb: A dream scheme, off the rubric: the cabins are not set on the land, they are the land. You turn in at the west notch between two glacial boulders and park on a gravel court, and from there you see almost no building at all, only a meadow rolling down to Mud Bay with grass roofs folded into it. The elders’ hollow (Elena & Tomas) is right beside the cars: a kidney-shaped cabin bermed into the hill on every side, entered at grade through a scooped entry court, so the walk from the car door to their sitting room is level the whole way; bedroom, accessible bath with a curbless shower and a stone-walled porch face south over the meadow. A lifted cedar boardwalk floats a couple of feet above the grasses, past the family longhouse, a long cedar house in the Coast Salish tradition whose back is buried to the eaves so its sod roof IS the hillside (you can walk straight off the meadow onto it): a gallery hall runs along the buried back wall, with Leo & Ana’s bunk room at the west end, a family hearth room in the middle and Maya & Ren at the water end, each opening through glass onto a long covered porch. Below it, the gathering hall is carved under the slope like Therme Vals: you step down into a sunk entry court, through a glass vestibule, into one long room whose only façade is a curved wall of glass to the bay, with a stone cave hearth at the west end and a terrace that wraps a ring of deck boards around the old madrone trunk. The boardwalk carries on over the bank to the twins’ bar, a slim cedar cabin threaded between two madrones, Daniel at one glass end and Sofia at the other, bath between. Runoff from the drive runs down a rill through three ponds (a rain garden by the notch, a reflecting pool under the hall’s glass, a cold plunge beside a little sod-roofed beach sauna). Firs and cedars screen the road. Well over 3,000 sq ft enclosed; rules off, so setbacks, lot width and the 1,600 sq ft cap are ignored.

schemes.name: F · Sky Datum
schemes.tag: dream scheme · rules off · lantern tower · glass pavilion on a mast · cable sky bridge · canopy pods · ribbon to a tidal pool · shell boathouse
schemes.blurb: A dream scheme that ignores the rubric (no sq ft cap, no setbacks, no height limit): the whole compound hangs off one level line in the air, the Sky Datum, 40 ft above the tide. You arrive at the west notch and walk a curving cedar ribbon across a granite arrival court to the foot of the Star Lantern, a 20-ft cedar octagon for Maya, Ren, Leo and Ana (bunk room and bath below, parents above) capped by a glass star dome and a railed rooftop deck for stargazing and watching orcas run down Mud Bay. From the lantern’s upper floor a cable-stayed sky bridge leaps 78 ft south-east, high over the meadow, to the Orca Glass: a glass teardrop gathering pavilion balanced on a single mast at the top of the bank, its shell roof curling up toward the water, kitchen and table for twenty floating in the treetops with nothing but bay in front of you. A second truss bridge threads straight through the crown of the big madrone to the Madrone Nest, a kidney-shaped pod on raking stilts that hugs the tree’s trunk, with Daniel’s and Sofia’s rooms either side of a bath. Elena and Tomas stay on the ground in the Moon House, a sod-roofed kidney on a slab right off the arrival court, step-free to their door, the firepit and the horizon pool on the bank edge. From the pavilion’s prow the Orca Leap, a ribbon bridge, swoops down over the bank and the beach to the Tide Pool, a ring of granite holding a sea-water pool out past the shoreline that fills on every high tide, next to the copper shell-roofed boathouse for kayaks.

schemes.name: G · Tide Shell
schemes.tag: rubric version of D · teardrop shell · kelp kidney · river stone · 1:20 ribbon walks
schemes.blurb: Arrive at the west notch and the drop-off sits level with the elders’ floor, so a railed boardwalk curls straight from the cars into their sitting room. Three buildings share one family of curved forms, all on the planner’s blob footprints. Family kelp kidney (532 sq ft) sits uphill and wraps a concave curve toward Mud Bay. Inside the curve every bedroom looks at the water from a crescent deck: Maya & Ren in the east lobe, Leo & Ana’s bunk room, a shared bath and linen closet, Daniel, and Sofia in the west lobe. A curving gallery and a domed entry porch face the uphill ribbon walk. Elders’ river stone (Elena & Tomas, 387 sq ft) is a sod-roofed pebble on a slab: sitting room with a stove, a bedroom opening onto a kidney porch, an accessible bath with a 60×60 curbless shower and a wardrobe. A level railed boardwalk runs from their sitting room across the rain-garden pond to the gathering cabin’s domed entry porch, so they move from car to home to dinner without a step. Gathering tide shell (601 sq ft) is a teardrop whose prow points down the bay under a copper shell roof that curls up toward the water. Entry, powder room and pantry sit at the round back; the kitchen is on the elders’ side, dining for 8 in the middle, and the lounge in the prow behind a 12-ft wrap-around slider. A broad cascade stair falls from the prow to the kidney tide-pool terrace, the firepit and a meandering beach path past the madrones. 1,520 of 1,600 sq ft enclosed, and every code check passes at the 35-ft reduced setback: shoreline clear by about 5 ft, lot-width 52 of 57 ft, tallest 20 ft, all four madrones kept.

schemes.name: H · Sod & Contour
schemes.tag: meets the rubric · three bermed sod-roof cabins · step-free from the car · sunk fire court
schemes.blurb: The earth-sheltered idea of E, tamed to the brief. You turn in at the west notch between two glacial boulders and park on a gravel court at the top of the lot, and the whole compound lies below you: three low cabins dug into the slope, backs bermed against the hill and roofs of living sod that read as part of the meadow, set side by side along one contour so together they use only 44 of the 57 ft the lot-width rule allows. The elders’ cabin (Elena & Tomas, 396 sq ft) is right off the parking. Its floor is set at the uphill grade, so a level gravel walk runs from the car door, under a sod-roofed porch, to their front door with no step at all. Inside, a foyer runs straight through the house; the sitting room and an accessible bath with a 60×60 curbless shower are on one side, the bedroom on the other, and a slider opens onto a covered south terrace. The family sleeping cabin (493 sq ft) is next along the walk, also entered at grade from the bermed back. A gallery hall runs along the earth wall under a strip of clerestory windows, and four bedrooms open off it on the view side: Daniel and Sofia each have their own room, Leo & Ana share the bunk room, and Maya & Ren have the water end, with a corner window and a slider onto the deck. The bath is off the hall. From there a graded walk (about 1:20, no steps) winds down the contours to the gathering cabin (616 sq ft), which is bermed into the hill behind and fully glazed toward the bay. You enter through a mudroom at the back, beside the pantry and powder room; the kitchen is on the west, with dining for 8 in front of it, a wood-stove hearth hall, and a lounge on the glass corner looking south-east down Mud Bay. The deck steps down to a flagstone fire court with boulder seats under a madrone, and a rain-garden pond catches the roof runoff. All four madrones are kept. 1,505 of 1,600 sq ft enclosed, and every code-check row passes at the 35-ft reduced setback.

schemes.name: I · Little Sky Datum
schemes.tag: meets the rubric · F scaled down · lantern tower · glass pavilion on a mast · level sky bridge · moon house
schemes.blurb: Scheme F brought down to earth and inside the rules. Arrive at the west notch and walk a curving cedar path from the drop-off to the Star Lantern, the family sleeping cabin: a 19-ft cedar octagon on two floors, Daniel’s and Sofia’s rooms and the bath on the ground floor, Maya and Ren’s room and Leo and Ana’s bunk room upstairs, and on the flat roof a railed star deck under an open glass-domed lantern for stargazing and orca-watching, 30 ft to the top of the dome. Down the lot sits the Orca Glass, the gathering cabin: a glass ellipse balanced on one central mast so its seaward side floats free of the slope, under a copper shell roof that curls up toward Mud Bay; kitchen and pantry against the uphill side, dining for 8 and the lounge along the glass facing the water, with a deck off the prow toward the firepit. Elena and Tomas live in the Moon House, a one-storey sod-roofed ellipse on a slab beside the arrival court, reached step-free on a gently graded path from the drop-off; their sitting room opens onto a short, level, cable-stayed sky bridge that lands on the pavilion floor at exactly the same height, so they get to dinner without a single step. Bedroom with wardrobe, accessible bath with 60×60 curbless shower, sitting room toward the bay. About 1,500 of 1,600 sq ft enclosed, all four madrones kept, 35-ft reduced shoreline setback from top of bank, under the lot-width rule and 35-ft height: every code check passes.
